what_it_does: Transformer models — the architecture behind most modern AI — are slow and memory-hungry because attention (the mechanism that lets every word look at every other word) scales quadratically with sequence length. Two tricks help: value-level sparsity (skipping multiplications whose results will be near zero anyway) and bit-level sparsity (using fewer bits to represent numbers, so each multiplication is cheaper). Combining both in the same chip creates a problem: different compute units end up with wildly unequal amounts of work, so most units sit idle while a few are overloaded. Libra is a chip design that pairs these two sparsity techniques with a hardware task-pool that dynamically redistributes work across compute units so they stay balanced, and it supports variable numerical precision within a single pass to make both tricks usable at once.
